issue_context.title: Stop applying the beta.kubernetes.io/os and beta.kubernetes.io/arch
issue_context.body:
It seems that according to plan, kubenrnetes 1.18 will remove support for the `beta.kubernetes.io/os` and` beta.kubernetes.io/arch` labels. Will we still do this work?

---

https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/kubernetes-api/labels-annotations-taints/
comments: If it needs to be removed in 1.18, I can try to contribute this code
@yujuhong  @liggitt

I would expect the following things to be done in order:
1. sweep for uses of the beta labels (in all kubernetes/kubernetes-sigs projects and documentation) in controllers/manifests/nodeSelectors and update them to the GA labels
2. in 1.19: update the node lifecycle controller to treat the GA os/arch labels as the authoritative source and copy them to the beta labels (flip the source of truth)
3. ~~in 1.19: update the kubelet to only set the GA labels~~ (delayed until we warn / verify selectors are mutable / notify users of beta labels / allow time with warnings to pass)
4. ~~no earlier than 1.22: update the node lifecycle controller to drop the beta labels if they differ from the GA labels~~

edit: before we stop setting beta labels, we should:
- [x] start warning on use of beta labels (done in 1.25 in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/108554)
- [ ] ensure all places beta labels can be used in node selectors support updating to GA labels (e.g. there are no immutable node selectors people could *not* change to GA)
- [ ] sweep public uses of beta [os](https://grep.app/search?q=beta.kubernetes.io/os) and [arch](https://grep.app/search?q=beta.kubernetes.io/arch) labels and file issues to update docs/manifests/code
- [ ] if all node selectors are mutable, no earlier than 1.28, stop setting beta labels on nodes

Got it, I can try to do the first stage first～～


/assign
/sig node
/reopen

These deprecated labels can be used in *many* places. Have we made the use of the deprecated labels sufficiently visible to users?

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/94626 tracks the places I know of where we have node selector / affinity / topology fields that could require updating.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/101688 starts to surface warnings for use of those labels in some objects (pod-spec-containing objects), but there are several others we have not given users warnings for.

I would expect us to make use of these deprecated labels _extremely_ visible for several releases, and give very clear guidance for how to change to use the GA labels in a non-disruptive way for each place they are used before dropping the beta labels, especially since the cost of maintaining them is relatively low.

/triage accepted
/area kubelet
/priority important-longterm
because of the backward compatibility constraint and the extra care involved, I don't think this is actually trivial

done, thanks for reminding me of my mistake

Wondering if the primary key switch should have happened one release before the beta label was removed from kubelet. 

I think this can potentially break some upgrade scenarios where kubelet runs on the control plane nodes. For example:
1. some critical daemonset (like CNI) uses node selector `beta.kubernetes.io/os`.
2. first control plane node is upgraded to v1.19 and kubelet only sets the GA label `kubernetes.io/os` now
3. kube-controller-manager is still running on v1.18 and is still expecting `beta.kubernetes.io` to be the source of truth
4. new v1.19 node is stuck in NotReady because it only has the kubernetes.io/os label and v1.18 kube-controller-manager is expecting beta.kubernetes.io/os to be the source of truth.

Ideally users should update their node selectors to use kubernetes.io/os though since that label will exist on both v1.18 and v1.19 nodes. The other workaround here is to restart the v1.18 kube-controller-manager pods and until the v1.19 kube-controller-manager is the leader.

Fwiw I don't think this technically violates version skew policy since the issue only occurs if you run a v1.19 kubelet when kube-controller-manager is still on v1.18, which is more common when you use kubelet static pods to run the control plane.
